title: Integer overflow — int, long and where sums blow up
summary: Ranges of int and long, the operations that overflow in DSA problems, Java's silent two's-complement wraparound, and safe patterns like mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2.
note:
1. Ranges
   • `int` ≈ ±**2.147·10⁹** · `long` ≈ ±9.22·10¹⁸
   • Two values up to 10⁹ fit (2·10⁹) — just; three don't
   • Java has no unsigned types; overflow wraps silently (two's complement), it never throws
2. Where it happens
   • Prefix sums / totals of many values
   • `mid = (lo + hi) / 2` → use `lo + (hi - lo) / 2`
   • `a * b` of two ints overflows **before** being stored → `(long)a * b`
   • Summing in an `int` accumulator → use a `long` accumulator (or `Arrays.stream(a).asLongStream().sum()`)
3. Spotting it
   • Wrong only on large tests, or negative results that should be positive
   • Default to `long` for sums, products and pair counts
✎ In my words: ______________________________________________

recall.q: Why does `long x = a * b;` still overflow for ints a, b?
recall.a: The multiplication happens in int before the widening conversion; cast first with `(long)a * b`.

recall.q: Does Java throw on integer overflow?
recall.a: No — int/long wrap around silently (two's complement). There are no unsigned types; use `Math.addExact` if you want a throw.

shot.title: Overflow checklist
shot.body:
| Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| sum of many values | `long` accumulator |
| `(lo + hi) / 2` | `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` |
| `a * b` with ints | `(long)a * b` |
| summing an int[] | `Arrays.stream(a).asLongStream().sum()` |
| counting pairs (n²) | `long` count |

sections.title: Ranges
sections.body:
✍️ `int` is 32-bit: about ±2.147·10⁹ (`Integer.MAX_VALUE` = 2,147,483,647).
✍️ `long` is 64-bit: about ±9.22·10¹⁸ (`Long.MAX_VALUE`).
✍️ Two values up to 10⁹ added together can exceed `int`. A product of two values up to 10⁵ (10¹⁰) exceeds `int`.
✍️ Java has **no unsigned integer types**; when an `int` overflows it wraps around (two's complement) and never throws — the bug is silent.

sections.title: Where it happens in DSA
sections.body:
✍️ Prefix sums of 10⁵ values up to 10⁴ → up to 10⁹, borderline; values up to 10⁹ → definitely `long`.
✍️ `mid = (lo + hi) / 2` overflows when lo + hi > 2·10⁹. Use `mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2`.
✍️ Multiplying `a * b` where both are `int` overflows **before** the result widens into a `long`. Write `(long)a * b`.
✍️ Binary search on the answer with a large `hi` (e.g. sum of weights) → make lo, hi, mid `long`.

sections.title: How to spot it
sections.body:
✍️ Wrong answer only on large tests, negative results that should be positive → overflow (the silent wraparound).
- Default to `long` for any sum, product, or count of pairs. It costs nothing in speed.
- When you want a crash instead of a silent wrap, `Math.addExact(a, b)` / `Math.multiplyExact(a, b)` throw `ArithmeticException` on overflow.
